input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: The structure of § 21 is otherwise sound: the cap is expressly mutual, the mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages is mutual, and the "Excluded Claims" definition already carries uncapped treatment for confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The cap basis, however, fails the fallback on a material term: "Fees" is defined (§ 1.5/1.6) as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, and the cap is further confined to the first Order Form, so the "twelve months" measure is illusory rather than 12 months of fees — walk-away territory for a vendor cap far below six months' fees. Our redline changes only the basis to lowercase fees paid or payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the event, leaving every other word intact. We have targeted the fallback; the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor and a broader "amounts due" payment carve-out (§ 21.3 currently ties the payment carve-out to the narrow defined "Fees") are noted but not pressed.

proposal.summary: Fix illusory cap basis: 12 months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap based on at least 12 months' fees, but "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, which makes the cap illusory. We have changed only the basis to fees paid or payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the event, leaving the mutual cap and the Excluded Claims carve-outs (indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) as drafted.
